prompt: An employee moves from Oregon to Washington mid-month but works remote for a New York company. Which taxes apply and from when?
system: You are a payroll assistant at a US company. Answer the request.
response:
# Remote Employee Moving from Oregon to Washington (New York Employer)

**Key principle:** For a remote employee, state taxes generally follow **where the work is physically performed and where the employee lives**, not where the employer is located. The **move date** is when obligations switch from Oregon to Washington.

## Summary Table

| Tax | Before move (OR resident, working in OR) | After move (WA resident, working in WA) |
|---|---|---|
| Federal income tax, Social Security, Medicare | Yes | Yes (no change) |
| FUTA (employer) | Yes | Yes (no change) |
| State income tax withholding | **Oregon** | **None** (WA has no income tax) |
| Oregon Statewide Transit Tax (0.1%, employee) | Yes | Stops |
| Paid Leave Oregon (employee and employer shares) | Yes | Stops |
| Oregon Workers' Benefit Fund assessment | Yes | Stops |
| Oregon local taxes (Metro SHS, Multnomah PFA, TriMet/Lane transit) | If the employee lived or worked in those districts | Stop |
| State unemployment (SUI) | **Oregon** | **Washington** (ESD) |
| WA Paid Family & Medical Leave | No | **Yes** (employee and employer shares) |
| WA Cares Fund (long-term care, employee-paid) | No | **Yes**, unless the employee has an approved exemption |
| WA workers' comp (L&I, state fund) | No | **Yes**. Employer must carry WA L&I coverage, and part is withheld from the employee |
| New York income tax, NY PFL, NY SDI | Generally **no** (see NY note) | Generally **no** |

## Timing: How to Handle the Mid-Month Switch

1. **Use the exact move date.** Treat it as the day the employee establishes WA residency and begins working from WA.
2. **Allocate by workdays in the straddle pay period.** Wages for days worked in Oregon are Oregon wages. Wages for days worked in Washington are Washington wages.
3. **Go by when the work was performed, not when it is paid.** If the first paycheck after the move covers days worked in Oregon, withhold Oregon tax on that portion. Oregon taxes nonresidents on Oregon-source wages.
4. **Allocate bonuses and commissions** by the period in which they were earned, typically by workday ratio.
5. **SUI wage base:** Washington generally lets you credit wages already reported to Oregon for the same employee in the same year toward the WA taxable wage base. Confirm this on your WA ESD reporting.

## New York Note: Convenience of the Employer Rule

New York can tax nonresidents who work from home "for their own convenience" when they are assigned to a New York office.

- **No NY tax:** If the employee is a genuinely remote hire who doesn't work in NY and isn't assigned to a NY office, NY withholding generally doesn't apply.
- **NY tax may apply:** If the employee is assigned to a NY office, or periodically works there, NY may claim tax on their wages, including remote days.
  - Before the move, Oregon would generally give the employee a credit for NY tax paid.
  - After the move, Washington has no income tax, so there's no offsetting credit. The NY tax would be a real cost to the employee.
- **Confirm the employee's assigned work location and NY travel** before deciding.

NY PFL, SDI, and UI follow the "localization" tests. They shouldn't apply if all work is performed in OR or WA.

## Action Checklist

- [ ] Get written confirmation of the move date and the new WA address.
- [ ] Update the payroll work location and residence effective on the move date.
- [ ] Stop Oregon withholding, transit tax, Paid Leave Oregon, and WBF after the final OR-sourced wages.
- [ ] Register in Washington, if you aren't already:
  - ESD for UI and PFML
  - L&I for workers' comp
  - Business Licensing Service / Department of Revenue, as needed
- [ ] Set up WA PFML and WA Cares deductions. Ask the employee whether they hold a WA Cares exemption letter.
- [ ] Report the employee's hours on WA ESD quarterly reports, since WA requires hours.
- [ ] File the final OR quarterly reports for this employee (OQ / Form 132) and close the OR accounts if no other OR employees remain.
- [ ] Prepare for two state lines on the W-2: OR wages for the pre-move period. Washington has no state income tax line.
- [ ] Remind the employee they'll file an **Oregon part-year resident return** (Form OR-40-P) for this year.

## Also Check

- **Local taxes after the move:** If the employee moves into Seattle, review whether the employer meets the threshold for the **Seattle JumpStart payroll expense tax**. This is employer-paid, not withheld.
- **Benefits and state-mandated leave:** WA paid sick leave and other employment-law requirements also start on the move date.

This is general payroll guidance. Rates and thresholds change annually, so verify current figures with each state agency, or consult a tax advisor on the NY convenience rule question.
